thread:
samir: FYI Acme saw intermittent 429s during a load spike earlier today. They say only some API keys get 429'd while others do not. Attaching quick curl that reproduced it and the response headers we captured. Ticket #12345 — can someone help triage whether this is key vs IP scoping?

marta: Can you paste the raw response headers and the request headers (esp X-Forwarded-For / immediate source IP)? Also include the request-id from the 429 responses.

samir: sure — here's the reproduction that reliably hits a 429 from our side (run from their proxy):

```bash
for i in {1..6}; do curl -s -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-abc123" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' & done
wait
```

Sample 429 response headers we got back:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
RateLimit-Limit: 120
RateLimit-Remaining: 0
RateLimit-Scope: ip
RateLimit-Reset: 22
X-Request-Id: rq_0a9f3b

And request headers showing proxy IP:
X-Forwarded-For: 34.112.145.67
Remote-Addr: 10.0.4.12 (internal)
Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-abc123

They said their outbound NAT was recently changed and multiple tenants are now egressing through a small NAT pool.

james: thanks — this smells like the IP-based bucket dominating despite a valid API key being present. There's a known precedence edge-case in the auth layer where if the proxy sets/overrides certain headers we end up resolving quota by IP first. Can you grab an auth-map lookup for that key and the NAT IP? e.g.:

```bash
# internal debugging endpoint
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-internal" "https://internal.redwood/quotas/lookup?key=sk-acme-abc123&ip=34.112.145.67"
```

We want to see which quota buckets are returned: api_key/project/org/ip. If the service returns ip-first that's our culprit. If you can't reach that endpoint, paste the auth service logs with request-id rq_0a9f3b.

jen: fyi cloudops did rotate the egress NAT pool yesterday for that region to cut cost on spare IPs — we condensed several prefixes into a smaller pool. That could cause multiple customers' keys to share the same public IP now. I'll roll a partial revert for the Acme CID range to confirm.

samir: grabbing the auth lookup now, attaching output snippet:

```
lookup_result: [
  { type: "ip", id: "34.112.145.67", bucket: "ip:shared-227", remaining: 0 },
  { type: "api_key", id: "sk-acme-abc123", bucket: "project:acme-project", remaining: 98 }
]
auth_decision: applied_bucket=ip:shared-227
```

So auth returned both, but the rate limiter applied the ip bucket (which is exhausted). Repro steps: run the earlier loop from behind the NAT with different keys vs same key — you'll see the ip bucket depletes and causes 429 even though the project's key has quota.

marta: that's important — customer experience wise we should prefer api_key/project buckets when an API key is present and only fallback to IP when no key is provided. Can eng propose a safe config change? Also set a temporary alert when ip-bucket-remaining < 10 so we catch cross-tenant NAT storms. :eyes: 

james: agree. Short-term mitigation: update quota precedence to prefer api_key > project > org > ip for requests carrying a recognized API key. I'll push a config flag to the rate-limiter and run smoke tests (non-prod first). If tests pass we'll flip in prod with a canary. Also adding a fast fallback rule: if ip-bucket is exhausted but api_key has remaining>0 then allow and decrement api_key bucket.

jen: rolling back the NAT condense for one /24 now for a customer test. I'll post when changes are in place.

samir: I'll update Acme with repro steps and ETA. Quick repro script for case comparison (run two processes, one using same key x6, another using 6 distinct keys from same NAT):

```bash
# repro: same key
for i in {1..6}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done; wait
# repro: distinct keys behind same NAT
for k in sk-acme-abc12{3..8}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $k" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done; wait
```

marta: perfect. Once eng config is staged, please also add a short-lived override so the customer's production traffic isn't blocked while we validate (set allow-if-key-has-quota=true).

support-bot: Ticket #12345 updated: priority -> high, assignee -> james (eng-oncall), watcher -> marta, cloudops.

james: I'll open an RFC to make precedence explicit and add unit tests. Will post the canary plan and rollback criteria here.

samir: thanks everyone — I'll follow up in the ticket after the NAT revert and canary.

marta: thanks — keeping customer looped in. :+1:
